description: Zinc is a chemical element with symbol Zn and atomic number 30. It is a slightly brittle metal at room temperature with a shiny blue whitish appearance when surface oxidation is removed, and is the first element in group 12 of the periodic table. It is the 24th most abundant element in Earth's crust.
uses: Zinc has major applications in hot-dip galvanization for plating corrosion-resistant coatings on iron, as well as use in electrical batteries, small non-structural casts, and alloys such as brass. A variety of zinc compounds are used in products including dietary supplements, deodorants, anti-dandruff shampoos, luminescent paints, and in chemical synthesis of organic compounds. Zinc is also an essential trace element for humans, animals, plants, and microorganisms, necessary for prenatal and postnatal development.
characteristics: Zinc is a bluish-white, lustrous, diamagnetic metal that is somewhat less dense than iron with a hexagonal crystal structure. It is hard and brittle at most temperatures but becomes malleable between 100 and 150 °C. Zinc has relatively low melting (419.53 °C) and boiling points (907 °C) for a metal, and is a fair conductor of electricity. It has five stable isotopes, with Zn-64 being the most abundant at nearly half of zinc's total abundance.
